head_commit.message:
Claude/actenon kernel mcp setup qolk0h (#2)

* fix: fail closed on shell expansions blastradius does not model

resolve_target only expands plain $VAR and ${VAR}. Any other expansion
left in the target after that pass — ${VAR:-/}, ${VAR:=/}, ${VAR:+x},
${#VAR}, ${VAR%pattern}, $1, $$, $@ — was passed through as a literal
filename and then judged in-scope, so it was ALLOWED. In a real shell
those forms produce a concrete path we never computed:

  rm -rf ${UNSET:-/}   # deletes / in bash; blastradius allowed it

This violates principle 2 (fail closed). Now, if a `$` survives variable
expansion, the target cannot be resolved with certainty and is refused
with a new unoverridable rule `unresolvable-expansion`. Plain $VAR /
${VAR} continue to expand normally, so in-scope deletions are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix: catch destructive commands behind wrappers and git global options

identify_destructive only inspected tokens[0], so any command runner in
front of rm hid it entirely. Every one of these was ALLOWED to hit a
floor path on main:

  sudo rm -rf /etc      env rm -rf /etc      xargs rm -rf /etc
  nice / nohup / setsid / exec / command / doas / busybox / ionice /
  stdbuf rm ...         timeout 5 rm -rf /etc     sudo rm -rf $HOME

Added _unwrap_wrappers(): it strips leading command-runner wrappers
(and their options/arguments, env NAME=VAL assignments, and the
timeout DURATION positional), recursing through nested wrappers, before
identification. It returns the tokens unchanged when the inner command
cannot be located, so unwrapping can only ever ADD a block, never remove
one. Applied to both identify_destructive and identify_risks.

Also fixed three narrower escapes:

- git global options before the subcommand (git -C / clean -fdx,
  git --git-dir=x --work-tree=/ reset --hard) hid the destructive
  subcommand from the args[0] == "clean"/"reset" check. Added
  _git_split() to parse global options and honour -C / --work-tree /
  --git-dir as the operative target directory.
- find -execdir rm was not detected (only -exec was).
- truncate with a glued size flag (truncate -s0 FILE) was not detected
  because the guard tested exact membership of "-s" in the flag list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* test: adversarial bypass regression suite (wrappers, git, expansions)

One test per confirmed bypass, each of which was ALLOWED on the parent
commit and is now a BLOCK: wrapper prefixes (F1), git global-option
escapes (F2), unmodelled shell expansions (F3), find -execdir (F4), and
truncate with a glued size flag (F5). Includes must-allow guards proving
the fixes do not over-block in-scope wrapped deletions or plain $VAR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* docs: correct README test count, rule table, and coverage notes

- The "128 tests" figure was stale (the suite is 198). Updated.
- Added the unresolvable-expansion rule to the rule reference table.
- Documented in the Identify/Resolve steps that command-runner wrappers
  are unwrapped, git global options are honoured, and expansions beyond
  $VAR/${VAR} are refused fail-closed — matching actual behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* ci: add test workflow running the suite on Python 3.10-3.12

The repo had only publish.yml (tags). Added ci.yml running the full test
suite on push/PR across the supported Python versions, matching the
sibling Actenon repos' Python CI style.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(eval-agent): make the isolation proof pass when run as root

The proof overlaid a tmpfs on /home to hide the host home canary, but a
root invocation has ~ = /root, which is not under /home, so TEST2
("host home canary is readable") failed. Overlay a tmpfs on the invoking
user's actual home directory as well, so the proof holds for any user.

head_commit.message:
v0.4.0: developer UX polish — severity tuning, --strict, --quiet, .env write-only

Five improvements from the v0.3.0 black-box evaluation:

1. pip install downgraded from high to medium severity.
   The eval found that pip install fires on every install — one of
   the most common developer commands. A high-severity warning on
   every pip install trains the developer to ignore all warnings.
   Now: medium severity for PyPI packages (· marker), high severity
   (⚠ marker) only for non-PyPI sources (git+ URLs, local paths).
   npm/yarn/cargo install also downgraded to medium.

2. --strict flag: treats warnings as blocks.
   blastradius --strict -- pip install stripe → exit 1
   For high-security environments or CI gates where any warning
   should stop execution. Without --strict, warnings are informational.

3. --quiet flag: suppresses the ALLOWED summary on safe commands.
   blastradius --quiet -- ls → no output (just the ls output)
   Warnings and blocks are still printed — --quiet only suppresses
   the one-line 'ALLOWED — 0 warnings' summary on commands that
   need no review.

4. .env detection: only warn on writes, not reads.
   cat .env → no warning (reading a secret file is less dangerous)
   sed -i 's/foo/bar/' .env → warning (writing to a secret file)
   echo '...' > .env → warning (creating a secret file)
   cp secrets .env → warning
   This eliminates false positives on developers reading config files.

5. Warning count in ALLOWED summary.
   'blastradius  ALLOWED — 0 warnings, filesystem-destruction check only'
   'blastradius  ALLOWED — 2 warning(s), not blocked.'
   The developer sees the count at a glance and knows whether to
   scroll up and read the warnings.

186 tests pass (was 185, +1 .env read/write distinction test).

head_commit.message:
v0.3.0: two-tier guard — blocks filesystem destruction, warns on everything else

The v0.2.0 black-box evaluation found that blastradius caught 5 of 14
consequential actions (36%) and missed the rest silently. The core
problem: silence on allow created a false sense of comprehensive
coverage. A developer who saw no output assumed the command was safe,
when in fact only filesystem deletion had been checked.

v0.3.0 fixes this with a two-tier architecture:

TIER 1 — BLOCK (filesystem destruction, unchanged):
  rm, rmdir, shred, truncate, dd, find -delete, git clean -f,
  git reset --hard. Floor rules and scope still unoverridable.

TIER 2 — WARN (non-filesystem consequential actions, NEW):
  - pip/npm/yarn/cargo install → [package] arbitrary code execution
  - curl/wget → [network] data exfiltration risk (escalates if credentials detected)
  - git filter-branch → [git] irreversible history rewrite
  - git push --force → [git] overwrites remote history
  - git push → [git] publishes commits (medium severity)
  - chmod -R / chown -R → [permission] recursive permission change
  - twine upload / npm publish → [publish] irreversible
  - .env / secrets / credentials access → [config] credential exposure
  - kubectl/terraform/ansible with production → [deployment] live infra
  - staging→production change → [deployment] verify intentional
  - ssh/scp/rsync → [network] remote system access
  - docker run -v → [deployment] host mount

Three UX changes:

1. ALLOWED commands now print a one-line summary:
   'blastradius  ALLOWED (filesystem-destruction check only)'
   Silence is never the output. The developer always knows the check
   ran and what scope it covered.

2. Commands with warnings print a WARNING block:
   'blastradius  WARNING'
   Each warning names the category, the reason, and the severity.
   The command is NOT blocked — the developer decides.

3. Compound commands (&&, ||, ;, |) are now SPLIT and each segment
   is checked independently. This removes the #1 false positive:
   'python -m build && twine upload dist/*' was refused in v0.2.0
   because && was unparseable. Now it's split into two segments,
   each checked, and the twine segment gets a [publish] warning.

Evaluation results (30 tasks, same test suite):

  Metric                     v0.2.0    v0.3.0
  consequential missed         9         0
  mean utility score          0.33      0.90
  tasks with utility ≥ 2       5        15
  false alarm rate            0%        0%

Every previously-missed action now gets a warning. Zero false alarms
on harmless tasks. The false positive on && is gone.

185 tests (was 160, +25 risk-warning tests). All pass.

workflow_runs.display_title: ci: add skip-existing to PyPI token fallback

head_commit.message:
ci: add skip-existing to PyPI token fallback

The v0.2.0 tag was published manually via twine (trusted publishing
isn't configured yet for this new PyPI project). When the publish
workflow then tried to upload the same version, PyPI returned 400
Bad Request (re-upload of existing version).

skip-existing makes the API-token fallback path idempotent: if the
version is already on PyPI, the step succeeds instead of failing.
This lets the workflow go green on a tag that was already published.

Trusted publishing (the preferred path) is unaffected — it only
fires when PYPI_API_TOKEN is not set, and a future work item should
configure it at pypi.org/manage/project/actenon-blastradius/settings/publishing/
so the token fallback is no longer needed.

head_commit.message:
v0.2.0: adversarial diligence round — 7 bugs fixed, 27 regression tests

Adversarial audit found 7 bugs ranging from critical to low. Every
one is fixed with a dedicated regression test in test_adversarial.py.

BUG 1 (critical) — Tokeniser refused ; | && even inside quotes.
  The refusal regex ran on the raw command string before quote-aware
  parsing, so rm -rf "foo;bar" was refused as a command separator.
  This caused false positives on any filename containing ;, |, &&.
  Fix: replaced the raw regex with a quote-aware character scanner
  that tracks single/double quote state and only flags metacharacters
  in unquoted context.

BUG 2 (critical) — Newline bypass: echo foo\nrm -rf $HOME allowed.
  The tokeniser treated \n as whitespace, producing a single token
  list. The command identifier saw 'echo' (non-destructive) and
  returned None. The second 'rm -rf $HOME' was never checked.
  An agent could bypass every check by sending a newline in the
  command string.
  Fix: newlines are now treated as command separators and refused
  with the unparseable-command-newline rule. Newlines inside quotes
  are still literals (correct).

BUG 3 (low) — Backslash-newline line continuation not handled.
  rm -rf /tmp/foo\\\nbar produced a token with a literal \n.
  Bash treats \\<newline> as a line continuation (removed).
  Fix: backslash-newline outside quotes is removed during
  tokenisation. Inside double quotes, same.

BUG 4 (medium) — rm -- -foo misclassified -foo as a flag.
  After --, bash treats every argument as a target, even if it
  starts with -. blastradius was not tracking --, so a file named
  -foo (or -rf) inside scope would not be checked.
  Fix: the flag/target parser now tracks the -- end-of-flags
  separator. Everything after -- is a target.

BUG 5 (medium) — rm -rf with no targets was allowed.
  An rm with no targets produced an empty target list, so no
  refusals were generated. The command was allowed.
  Fix: destructive commands with zero targets are now refused
  with the no-targets rule.

BUG 7 (medium) — os.execvp crash on command-not-found.
  When the command was allowed but the binary didn't exist,
  os.execvp raised FileNotFoundError and the user saw a Python
  traceback.
  Fix: catch FileNotFoundError (exit 127) and PermissionError
  (exit 126) with clean error messages.

BUG 8 (medium) — /path/** did not match /path itself.
  The ** glob required at least one path component after the
  prefix. rm -rf /tmp/blast_repo (the repo root itself) was
  out-of-scope even though scope allowed /tmp/blast_repo/**.
  Fix: the ** regex now matches zero path components, so
  /tmp/blast_repo/** matches both /tmp/blast_repo and
  /tmp/blast_repo/foo.

Test suite: 160 tests (was 133, +27 adversarial). All pass.
Decision time still sub-millisecond.

head_commit.message:
rename PyPI package to blast-radius (blastradius was taken)

The PyPI name 'blastradius' is registered by an unrelated Terraform
dependency-graph visualisation tool (Patrick McMurchie, v0.1.23).
Renamed the distribution to 'blast-radius' (available). The import
name and CLI command remain 'blastradius' — only the pip/uvx name
changes:

  pip install blast-radius
  uvx blast-radius -- rm -rf /tmp/foo
  blastradius -- rm -rf /tmp/foo   # command unchanged

Also adds .github/workflows/publish.yml using the same trusted-
publishing (OIDC) pattern as Actenon's other repos, with API-token
fallback via PYPI_API_TOKEN secret. Triggers on tag push (v*).

133 tests still pass. Wheel and sdist rebuilt and verified.
